transcript_tail.text: Now the user-background memories for the raw resume material.
I have the full picture now. Let me check what git ignores (the resume will eventually hold contact PII) before deciding where to put the draft.

I have everything I need. This is a greenfield task — no resume exists yet. My plan: draft the full resume + LinkedIn rewrite now — writing in full the parts I can (positioning, the two-project platform, skills) and leaving clearly-marked `[FILL: …]` slots for facts only you have. That gives you a concrete draft to react to (resume feedback is the next step in `notes/network-outreach.md`) and surfaces exactly what's missing. Let me build it.
Now let me reflect the work in this session's title so it's visible in the session list.
`--self` keys off cwd; from the ai-harness dir it can't see the worktree. Let me pass the CSE id explicitly.

Drafts are in place and the session is retitled `[JOB] Resume + LinkedIn rewrite`. Here's what I built under `resume/`:

- **`resume/resume.md`** — full resume draft. Written in full: the summary, the DS Trader + FamilyFund platform section (your differentiator), and skills. Skeleton-with-bullets for the experience section.
- **`resume/linkedin.md`** — headline (3 lanes incl. a discreet "still at Visa" option), About (first-person, leads with the platform hook), experience reframes, Featured, and the *Open to Work* settings.
- **`resume/README.md`** — the locked positioning (builder-first, rules-based, *not* AI-framed, startup audience) and the full list of `[FILL: …]` gaps.

The positioning is fully baked per your memory: builder/tech-lead first, projects as strong *general* engineering (no AI-flagship framing), AI/ML kept as career *direction* only, no big-co language, DS Trader strictly rules-based.

What's left is the career facts only you have — Visa accomplishments, the earlier company names/dates, education. The fastest way to fill those well is for me to mine an existing document rather than interview you slot-by-slot.
